status: PRE-REGISTERED: committed before the successor module, its tests and its replay existed, and before the predecessor code ran on the new fixture. Not edited after results are seen; post-run notes go to REPORT.md.
scope: a minimal successor of the predecessor's report(): the same parsers, rule, fixtures and wheels; three targeted changes only; structural evidence for triage, never admission

targeted_changes.T1_text_oracle: remove the html5lib_text_rule_equals_itertext consistency requirement (ElementTree's C-accelerated itertext yields comment payloads, so it is not the intended rule) and add an independent oracle: for each tree, a structure-only lxml copy of the unit (every element becomes <e>, every comment <!--c-->, every PI <?p?>, with the original text and tail strings, the final unit element's tail cleared) inside one container, whose libxml2 XPath string() is the oracle text. It shares no code with the rule function. Equality with the rule is a consistency check; itertext is kept only as an observation (equals rule; equals rule with comment payloads) and never produces a finding
targeted_changes.T2_axes: keep STRUCTURE_CORROBORATED/REVIEW as the structural axis only (same rule as the predecessor); report the pinned helper's reasons and status unchanged on their own axis; add consumer_gate = NOT_GRANTED to every report with an explicit prohibition (no admission, no fit to any caller's prompt or size limit, no semantic sufficiency, no permission to dispatch a model); replace the predecessor replay's R9 with the property the contract states (see corrected_R9)
targeted_changes.T3_scope: state in every report and in REPORT.md exactly what the comparison covers and what it does not; no comparison rule is relaxed: every parser error, ambiguity, encoding disagreement and structural difference stays REVIEW; no global diagnostic is whitelisted; the exact-id rule is unchanged

comparison_scope: compared between the two trees: encoding (codec name); exact id matches (count) and the rule's structural reasons; for a selected unit: membership (signature ids, signature and description counts, anchor position, nested object ids), boundaries (dl and its parent as kind/name/id/class, the kinds and names of all dl children, the unit's element indexes, neighbouring elements, enclosing object id), ordered topology of the unit (depth, node kind, mapped name and only the id, class and href attributes of each node), links (href and text of each a), and the exact concatenated unit text. Not compared: any other attribute (title, lang, style, data-*, ...), comment and PI payloads, where text sits inside the unit (only the concatenation), anything outside the unit and its dl, the document head, and the full DOM. Parser diagnostics and errors are not compared with each other; any of either makes REVIEW.
text_rule: unchanged from the predecessor: text(element) = element.text + for each child in order: text(child) + child.tail, with text(comment or pi) = '' (payload excluded, tail kept); unit text = text(e_i) + tail(e_i) for every top-level unit element except the last, whose tail is excluded

mutation_controls.note: deliberately wrong text functions, applied to the same unit nodes; the oracle must differ from each (detected) while it equals the correct rule
mutation_controls.M1_comment_payload_included: comment and PI payloads counted as text
mutation_controls.M2_comment_tail_dropped: the tail after a comment or PI omitted
mutation_controls.M3_final_tail_included: the last unit element's tail appended
mutation_controls.M4_inter_unit_tail_dropped: tails between top-level unit elements omitted
mutation_controls.undetectable_note: W1 has no comment or PI, so M1 and M2 equal the correct rule there; they are recorded, not counted as failures

corrected_R9.historical: predecessor scripts/replay.py lines 95-98: prop('R9 a helper REVIEW is never upgraded', all(s == 'OK_STRUCTURAL_UNIT' for s in statuses) or rep['triage']['disposition'] == 'REVIEW'). It requires REVIEW whenever any helper status is not OK, which the predecessor's disposition_rule does not state (that rule names no helper status), so it is stronger than the contract.
corrected_R9.successor: R9 (corrected): (a) existing_helper.reasons and existing_helper.status are those of the pinned select_unit(), unchanged and reported on their own axis; (b) if the helper has any reason (structural or PARSER_DIAGNOSTICS_PRESENT), the structural disposition is REVIEW; (c) consumer_gate.value is NOT_GRANTED in every report. A helper status of REVIEW_OVER_BUDGET may coexist with STRUCTURE_CORROBORATED, which is then the structural axis only.

regression.cases: the predecessor's eight cases (research/public-sphinx-parser-corroboration-20261018-01/fixtures/expectations.json), same fixtures, anchors and locators, run once after the change
regression.unchanged_fields: per case, compared strictly with the predecessor's committed report (only environment.python, .platform, .machine exempt): environment, anchor, source, decoding_policy, parsers, name_mapping, existing_helper, trees, comparison.agreements, comparison.findings without CONSISTENCY_CHECK_FAILED, the four checks lxml_parse_diagnostics_equal_helper / mirror_reasons_equal_helper / mirror_membership_equals_helper / lxml_text_rule_equals_helper_text_content, and the disposition (predecessor triage.disposition = successor structural_corroboration.disposition)
regression.changed_fields: request_id; checks: html5lib_text_rule_equals_itertext removed, lxml_text_rule_equals_oracle and html5lib_text_rule_equals_oracle added; new: observations.itertext, text_ledger, comparison_scope, consumer_gate, structural_corroboration (replacing triage); C2 only: CONSISTENCY_CHECK_FAILED leaves comparison.findings
regression.oracle_checks: true for every unit in both trees (N1-N5, C1, C2); not applicable for C17 (no unit)
regression.itertext_observation: html5lib: C2 itertext differs from the rule and equals the rule with comment payloads included (C accelerator, Linux 3.12.3); every other unit equal; lxml: recorded without prediction

c1_html5lib_errors.rationale: html5lib 1.1 html5parser.py endTagBlock (lines 1349-1353 in the retained wheel): it computes inScope, and then parseError('end-tag-too-early') whenever the current node is not the closed element, whether or not that element is in scope; at the div was already closed by the implied , so the current node is the second dd. Observed on Linux (predecessor logs/10) and reported for macOS by the user.

dependencies: the predecessor's retained wheels, imported through zipimport (PYTHONPATH = the three .whl files, each sha256-checked at run time); an existing lxml (Linux: 6.1.3 with libxml2 2.14.6); no install and no download
